passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Rosetta Stone was found in Egypt in 1799.
• It carries the same official decree written in three scripts.
• The scripts are Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and ancient Greek.
• Scholars could read Greek, which helped them decipher the hieroglyphs.
stem: The student wants to explain why the Rosetta Stone was valuable to scholars. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Because the stone repeats one text in Greek and in hieroglyphs, scholars used the Greek to decipher the hieroglyphs.
The Rosetta Stone, which was found in Egypt in 1799, carries an official decree that is written in three different scripts.
The three scripts on the Rosetta Stone are Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic, and ancient Greek.
Scholars in the early 1800s could read ancient Greek, which was one of the scripts on the stone.
steps: "Why it was valuable" needs a reason.
The reason: the same text in a known language (Greek) and an unknown one (hieroglyphs).
Only one choice links the two scripts to deciphering.
The others describe the stone or the scripts without saying why that mattered.
key: Goals with "explain why" need a because-style answer, not just facts.
source: SAT AIS original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
